transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10
Time: 14:00 PT / 21:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Recording ID: ff-2026-09-10-7862-marigold

Auto-summary (auto-generated): QBR-style check in. Usage up 63% YoY but July spike caused cost overrun; three short incidents with degraded latency on peak windows. Customer wants private deployment guardrails and security artifacts before commit.

[00:00] Samira Patel (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Samira from Redwood, with Diego (SE) and Hannah (CSM). How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Alicia Chen (Head of ML): Good, thanks. Busy month. Appreciate the readout.
[00:15] Tom Baker (VP Eng): Hey thanks, we'll try to keep it tight.

[02:00] Diego Ruiz (SE): Quick agenda: usage/cost trends, incidents recap, options for Dedicated vs Private, security questions, and then next steps. I have some numbers ready.
[02:15] Marcus Li (SRE): Cool. We pulled the spike logs — want to see the tail latencies.

[04:10] Diego Ruiz (SE): Right. So overall usage increased 63% year-over-year, for Marigold specifically your token volume doubled between June and August. The July spike — looks like an exploratory campaign and a prompt set change — caused CPU/GPU contention and batching penalties. We saw average p95 token latency increase from ~220ms to ~410ms during the peak windows.
[04:35] Alicia Chen: That aligns with our internal spike, we rolled an aggressive prompting template. The hallucination checks were failing so we tightened sampling which I think ballooned tokens.
[05:05] Samira Patel: Makes sense. The cost side — your July invoice had a notable overrun. We can itemize the per-token and per-request drivers and propose rate caps.
[05:20] Tom Baker: We'd like proposals that make costs predictable; engineering wants latency SLAs though. We're worried about toggling batching because it can change response time variability.

[07:00] Diego Ruiz: Tradeoffs: continuous batching helps unit cost but can add queuing latency tail. Options: dedicate a small Reserved pool for your critical routes (can be Dedicated or Private) where we enforce low-latency policies, and use hosted for lower-priority traffic.
[07:25] Marcus Li: Can we do autoscale for dedicated pool? We can't have sustained idle cost.
[07:35] Diego Ruiz: Yes, Redwood Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and burst pool. You can also set min/max instance counts. For Private VPC we can recommend right-sized kernels and quantized variants to keep cost down.

[09:45] Priya Nair (Security): Quick cut — we need SOC2 and KMS info before moving to any pilot with customer data. Also log retention and audit trails are blockers for our compliance team.
[10:05] Hannah Lee (CSM): Understood. We'll share our SOC2 summary and KMS integration note. Samira will own that share.
[10:20] Samira Patel: Yup, I'll drop redacted SOC2 artifacts and an architecture note on KMS/HSM. Also, we capture audit logs per-request — retention configurable.

[12:30] Alicia Chen: For the pilot, we'd want to evaluate both latency and regression in output (we saw slight degradation after quantization in another provider). Can Redwood run a head-to-head benchmark with our test prompts?
[12:50] Diego Ruiz: Absolutely. We can run a 48-hour benchmark using your prompt set, measuring p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost, and a basic quality pass rate (exact-match or hallucination summary). We'll deliver the runner script and results.

[15:15] Tom Baker: How do you handle model fallbacks? If a dedicated instance gets saturated, will requests go to hosted variants? We need graceful degrade not 500s.
[15:35] Diego Ruiz: We have smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants by policy. For Dedicated we can configure a soft-fallback to a slightly smaller variant or route to another region. We'll also set circuit-breakers and user-visible status so you can handle degraded responses on the client side.

[18:00] Marcus Li: Network egress — if we go VPC private, what are the egress patterns? We need to keep traffic within our region for residency.
[18:20] Samira Patel: With Redwood Private you control the VPC peering and can restrict egress; region locking is supported for private deployments. We'll need the topology to ensure we match your RGW/NAT constraints.

[20:40] Alicia Chen: On the cost side, can you show us a 3-month Dedicated pricing vs hosted expected spend? We want to compare unit economics.
[21:00] Samira Patel: Yes, we'll prepare a pilot pricing proposal: a 3-month Reserved pool sized to your p95 peak with burst capacity and a blended rate. If the benchmark looks good we'll include a conversion path to Private deployment.

[23:15] Tom Baker: One more: model versions. We need pinning and rollout safety. Our compliance team won't accept silent changes to model behavior.
[23:30] Diego Ruiz: You can pin model versions and Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic rollback policies if quality metrics regress. We'll wire the eval suite to gate rollouts.

[26:05] Priya Nair: About logs — are request payloads stored? We can't have PII persisted.
[26:20] Hannah Lee: By default hosted stores request metadata for billing; content storage is configurable. For Private we can configure no-persistence and only deliver ephemeral KV caches. We'll document the options.

[28:45] Alicia Chen: Great. On quality, quantization caused a small spike in hallucinations for our NLU intents in an A/B test with another provider. Can Redwood run quantization experiments and show the delta?
[29:05] Diego Ruiz: Yes, we'll include quantized variants in the benchmark and measure quality delta using your prompts. We can also run mixed-precision and 4-bit vs 8-bit comparisons.

[32:00] Marcus Li: For benchmarking, what telemetry will you share? We need token-level cost, latency histograms, trace IDs for mapping to our distributed traces.
[32:15] Diego Ruiz: We'll provide token-level cost CSVs, latency histograms, p50/p95/p99, and trace hooks with the trace ID mapping. We'll also share the runner so you can reproduce locally.

[35:00] Tom Baker: Timeline for pilot? We have an initiative to decide by the end of Q3.
[35:10] Samira Patel: Tight but possible. Proposed: benchmark this week (Diego runs, needs prompts), get security docs in by Monday, pricing draft by next Wednesday, and follow-up on 2026-09-24 to finalize SOW.

[38:10] Alicia Chen: That works. We'll deliver prompts and network topology by Friday.
[38:30] Priya Nair: Also copy legal — they want a standard DPA and clarity on subprocessor list.
[38:45] Hannah Lee: We'll attach our DPA template and subprocessor list; Samira will confirm.

[41:00] Diego Ruiz: Quick note on mitigation for July spike — we recommend: 1) add request rate limiting on exploratory prompts, 2) set a dedicated pool for critical routes, 3) enable prefix caching for common completions to reduce repeated tokens. These three often cut cost spikes by 35-50%.
[41:30] Marcus Li: Prefix caching sounds useful — how intrusive is that to implement?
[41:40] Diego Ruiz: Minimal; it's a configuration and small client-side change to attach a cache key. We'll include docs.

[44:00] Samira Patel: Recap / next steps: Diego runs the benchmark (48 hours) once we get prompts; I'll send SOC2 + KMS notes; pricing pilot in 3-month band; schedule 2026-09-24 to review. Action items will be shared in an email after this. Anything else?
[44:25] Tom Baker: No, thanks. Appreciate the thoroughness.
[44:35] Alicia Chen: Thanks everyone.
[44:45] Priya Nair: Thanks.
[44:50] Samira Patel: Great, we'll follow up. Bye.

End of transcript.
